params.why: the missing value must be a clean whole number between 1 and 20, in the same range as the book's data

stem: The following is a list of data: ${=a}; {=b}; {=c}; {=d}; {=e}; x$. Determine the value of $x$ if the mean of all six values is ${=m}$.
solution: The mean is the sum of the values divided by how many values there are. This list has 6 values, counting $x$.
Add the values we know: ${=a}+{=b}+{=c}+{=d}+{=e}={=known}$. The sum of all six values is therefore $x+{=known}$.
notes: Basic-tier entry point of the skill, modelled on book question ex10-7-25d (list of data with an unknown x, mean given, page 387; book answer 10 from x + 38 = 48). Skeleton: five known values drawn from 1 to 15 (repeats allowed, as in the book's 8; 8), one unknown x placed last, a stated mean of all six values. Working: total = mean x 6, then x = total - sum of known values. The mean m is drawn AFTER the five values from the range that forces x between 1 and 20, so there is no rejection sampling and every instance has a whole-number answer; the require is a safety net only. The stem says 'mean of all six values' so the count is unambiguous. Numeric answer, so no distractors and no catalogued misconception is attached: the two catalogued misconceptions (mode not the most frequent value, median found without ordering) belong to the mode and median parts of this objective, which a mean-only basic item does not touch. The standard tier (book's remove-friends-and-find-the-total questions ex10-2-6 to ex10-2-11, the missing jar) and the advanced tier (mean plus median or mode, ex10-7-25c) are outside the gap list given and are not written here.
